transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~53 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Lucent Head of AI), Owen Carter (Cloud Eng), Sofia Morales (Security), Ethan Li (Dev), Maya Patel (Product)

Summary:
- Lucent is evaluating integration options between Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for an internal assistant and document search use cases. Primary constraints: latency under 300ms for short queries, strict data residency for some EU customers, and SSO/KMS requirements.
- Focus areas covered: SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy and network topology, rate limits/quotas and burst behavior, and observability hooks (tracing / logs / cost per route).

Topics:
- SDKs, examples, and code snippets (Python/TypeScript)
- LangChain / LlamaIndex adoption patterns and adapter workarounds
- Gateway/proxy architecture and on-prem network considerations
- Rate limits, quotas, and per-route throttling
- Observability integrations: traces, metrics, token cost breakdowns

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: okay everyone hi thanks for joining, i'm jamie with Redwood Inference, i'll kick off, we got about 50 minutes, happy to do deep dive on integration stuff.
[00:18] Priya Desai: hey jamie, thanks, we briefed the team — high level we want to understand how Redwood fits into our infra, we have a mix of cloud-hosted services and some on-prem datacenters in frankfurt for eu data. wondering about hosted vs dedicated vs private options.
[00:36] Marco Ruiz: sure, quick product callout — hosted is our managed api for fastest time-to-value, dedicated = reserved GPU pools with tenancy, private = customer-managed control plane (vpc/on-prem). we'll walk through SDKs and typical gateway setups.
[00:50] Owen Carter: quick network question — can we put a gateway in front of Redwood hosted endpoints? like corporate proxy with whitelist?
[01:05] Marco Ruiz: yes, you can front with a gateway/proxy, typical pattern is corporate egress to Redwood public api, we support mutual TLS and ip allowlists for dedicated customers, for private you'd run the control plane inside your vpc. sometimes folks terminate TLS at the gateway and use internal auth — depends on security posture.
[01:30] Sofia Morales: KMS — we require customer-managed keys for model inputs persistence. is that possible on hosted?
[01:43] Jamie Chen: hosted currently offers encryption at rest and enterprise KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we have bring-your-own-key options for enterprise plans — i'll send the exact security whitepaper, but short answer: BYOK for dedicated/private is straightforward, hosted BYOK for certain tiers.
[02:05] Ethan Li: for SDKs, we use python and node, and heavily rely on LangChain and LlamaIndex. how is the compatibility story?
[02:20] Marco Ruiz: we have first-class SDKs in python and ts, plus community adapters. For LangChain, standard llm wrappers work, for LlamaIndex there are connector examples — note sometimes you need to map streaming chunks differently because of our streaming API semantics. i'll share code snippets.
[02:45] Priya Desai: any gotchas with Llama Index chunking / embeddings? our pipelines do local chunking plus embeddings before upserting.
[02:58] Marco Ruiz: embeddings are supported as a separate endpoint; you can batch them, and we surface per-embedding cost and latency metrics. watch for rate limit on large batch sizes — we recommend batching to 512 items but tune by model. also note quantized models might change latency profiles.
[03:20] Maya Patel: are there official LangChain/LLamaIndex examples? we don't want to invent the integration.
[03:30] Jamie Chen: yes — repo: github.com/redwood-inference/examples langchain-llamaindex. i'll share link. includes retriever + streaming generator flows and an example proxy config.
[03:45] Owen Carter: about rate limits — we need predictable burst for customer-facing endpoints. what happens when we exceed quotas? can we have per-route quotas and graceful degradation?
[04:02] Marco Ruiz: yes, we support per-api-key and per-route quotas. For dedicated customers you can push higher burst windows. policy-based fallbacks are supported — e.g., on quota hit you can route to a cheaper model variant or to a cached response. built-in 429 behavior plus headers that indicate remaining tokens/time window.
[04:30] Priya Desai: observability — we need tracing into our existing APM, as well as token-level cost breakdowns per query.
[04:42] Marco Ruiz: we export request traces and timing breakdowns. you can instrument with OpenTelemetry; we can push traces to your collector or provide logs to a private s3. Console shows per-route token and latency dashboards. also have hooks for structured metadata to be passed as attributes for downstream correlation.
[05:05] Sofia Morales: audit logs and compliance — do you log prompts? retention controls?
[05:15] Jamie Chen: retention controls are configurable per-workspace; redact options exist. For private/deployed control plane you keep logs in your vpc; hosted we provide retention policies and an audit log export. we'll attach SOC2 summary.
[05:35] Ethan Li: micro-benchmarking — we'd like to run a latency/cost micro-benchmark on our typical prompt set. what do you need from us?
[05:50] Marco Ruiz: best is to share a small prompt corpus and expected QPS + p95 targets; we can spin a short test on Dedicated or hosted sandbox. i'll prepare a checklist (payload size, anchor prompts, concurrency, preferred models).
[06:10] Jamie Chen: timeline wise — priya is there a timeline or procurement window?
[06:18] Priya Desai: aim to decide by end of q2 for pilot, procurement by august if pilot is successful. security review is a gating item.
[06:30] Jamie Chen: great, we'll prioritize sending security docs.

-- Mid-call deep dive (architecture) --
[18:12] Marco Ruiz: if you're running a corporate gateway, common setup is: internal services -> gateway/proxy (auth + routing) -> Redwood API (hosted) or -> Private deployment endpoint in your VPC. For Dedicated, it's more like gateway -> dedicated endpoint with ip allowlist. A note on kv cache: we call it KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV catch) — it's important for prefix caching when you have repeated context windows.
[18:40] Owen Carter: do you expose a local sidecar for caching or is it handled server-side?
[18:50] Marco Ruiz: the runtime handles kv/prefix caching server-side; you can also run a local proxy cache for extreme latency needs. sidecar is community supported pattern.
[19:05] Priya Desai: about model variants — we want to test cheaper quantized variants for high-volume low-latency paths. how transparent are those?
[19:20] Marco Ruiz: we offer model profiles and quantization recommendations per workload. routing policy can fallback to quantized variant automatically, and we surface quality regression metrics tied to eval sets.
[19:36] Ethan Li: any limitations on streaming via proxies? sometimes we see chunk reassembly issues.
[19:45] Marco Ruiz: streaming is supported end-to-end, but proxies that buffer can add latency; recommend proxy passthrough for streaming endpoints and htt/2 or websocket based transports. we have example nginx/haproxy configs in the repo.

-- Security deep-dive --
[28:03] Sofia Morales: SSO/saml and RBAC — we need SSO for console and api key provisioning, and strict RBAC for routes.
[28:20] Jamie Chen: supported — SAML/SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC granular roles in Console. For API-level access you can bind api keys to roles and set per-route permissions.
[28:40] Sofia Morales: logging of prompts to audit trail is sensitive — can we disable raw prompt logging?
[28:50] Marco Ruiz: yes, redaction toggles exist; plus field-level redaction. for highest compliance customers we recommend Private deployment where logs never leave your network.

-- Integration details / code snippets --
[35:10] Marco Ruiz: (reads example) python example: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client.responses.stream(...). LangChain example: use RedwoodLLM wrapper in chain with streaming callbacks. In LlamaIndex you need to adapt the index builder to use our embeddings endpoint directly. I'll paste these in the followup.
[36:00] Ethan Li: any rate limit headers we should expect?
[36:10] Marco Ruiz: yes x-rw-rlimit-remaining, x-rw-rlimit-reset, and token-cost headers for per-response accounting.
[36:25] Priya Desai: observability, will it integrate with datadog? we use datadog + honeycomb.
[36:35] Marco Ruiz: datadog is supported via metric exporters; we can also push traces to your otel collector for honeycomb.

-- Pricing/ops and wrap up --
[45:55] Jamie Chen: pricing summary — hosted is usage-based per-token + embeddings; dedicated has reserved capacity and lower unit costs; private is enterprise licensing. We'll send a pilot pricing sheet.
[46:10] Priya Desai: do you support trial credits for benchmarking?
[46:18] Jamie Chen: yes, we'll provision a test api key for the sandbox with limited quota.
[46:30] Owen Carter: final question — for eu data residency can we pin model host region?
[46:40] Marco Ruiz: yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted enterprise customers can request region controls.

[50:02] Jamie Chen: recap of next steps: we will send SDK examples + langchain/llamaindex repo link, security whitepaper + SOC2 summary, provision sandbox api key, and marco will send benchmark checklist. Priya will share prompts and success criteria.
[50:25] Priya Desai: thanks, that timeline works, i'll aim to share prompts by wednesday.
[50:35] Jamie Chen: perfect, we'll follow up via email and add these as action items. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
